newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen rebounding at mid-week.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen rebounding at mid-week.

text.p: Polish shares should extend their current two-session, profit-taking fall early next week but could rebound at mid-week before firms release their September earnings reports, analysts said on Friday.

Firms recorded slightly better earnings in July and August after an unspectacular first half and analysts said the stable September industrial climate indicator released last week suggested the firms' earnings that month might prove good too.

"The overall business climate seems better and two (parallel market) firms that already released their earnings -- Dom-Plast and Amerbank -- showed good numbers," said Grzegorz Pinder of Bank Staropolski brokerage.
The main market's WIG index rose 1.7 percent this week to 14,920.4 points. It has surged more than 90 percent this year.

Analysts said recent gains on the Polish exchange were apparently linked with bourse records abroad, and that more foreign demand might be forthcoming this quarter as Western investment funds increased buying in the region.
Until then analysts said the current correction should take the market down to around 14,600 points, though Pinder said the WIG could drop as low as 13,500.
"That would not be such a big correction considering we just reached 15,000 points," Pinder said, reffering to the market's 30-month high at 15,078.7 points on Wednesday.
Analysts also said investors would watch Tuesday's September year-on-year inflation figure, which the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, sees around 19 percent.
"Only a number above 20 percent would be harmful for the market," said Ryszard Wojnowski of Bank Gdanski brokerage.
But analysts expected no quick interest rate cut as the NBP has said it wants real rates to rise in the coming months.
Analysts said the main market's top gainer, Remak, rose 10.5 percent this week after having revised up its first-half net profit figure by 65 percent.
They said biggest loser Rolimpex dropped 5.6 percent after revising down its first-half profit to 12.9 million from 16.3 million zlotys.
Analysts also said Budimex could be boosted next week after having won a 188-million-zloty sewage-treatment tender for the northern port city of Gdansk.
